- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, model overestimates — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.3–0.7) — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5 days.
- If forecast is >10% above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or falling.
- Model shows lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment rises sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period prices — cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome if sentiment is weak or flat.
